reason: I want to build the skin's supporting layer; the fibers and support cells seem suited to that role.
expectation: I expect a connective support tissue for the skin, though I'm unsure what it will be called.

alternatives.reason: Joining surface cells also seems relevant to the skin goal, but I chose to build its support first.

reaction: The tug panels make the fibers’ supporting role clear.
reason: Joining surface cells seems like a useful next step toward a protective skin border.
expectation: I expect a connected sheet of surface cells, though it may still need the tough outer layer.

reaction: The tug and seam make the junctions’ role clear.
reason: Adding the tough outer layer should build the skin’s protective border.
expectation: I expect a more protective surface layer that may still need to be joined to the supporting layer.

reaction: The distinction between the dead surface and living layers is interesting and clear.
reason: Joining the barrier to its support should bring the skin layers together.
expectation: I expect a layered skin structure that will still need sensory endings to detect contact.

reaction: The supply route across the layers is a useful detail.

reaction: The touch signal arrows make the skin’s sensing role clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and connecting the supply network should help sustain the working arm.
expectation: I expect an arm supplied with oxygen and nutrients; it may still need the sensitive skin attached for protection.

effect: The supply network and arm formed a supplied arm, with vessels shown beside its muscles and bones. The sensitive skin can now be added.
reaction: The separate vessel and nerve lines help distinguish supply from control.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and adding the skin should protect the supplied arm and give it touch sensation.
expectation: I expect a protected, touch-sensitive arm that may be ready to interact with the glass.

effect: Adding sensitive skin created a living body model and revealed the goal of using contact feedback to hold the glass steady.
reaction: Seeing the arm connected to the supporting body systems brings the earlier constructions together.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and using the glass with the model should address the new goal.
expectation: I expect the model to grasp and hold the glass using touch feedback, though I am unsure how the result will show that.

effect: The glass result completed the goal and showed how touch signals can lead to an adjustment in muscle force when the glass begins to slip.
reaction: The slipping glass made the feedback loop concrete and satisfying to see.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using the body model to hold the glass brought the skin, nerves and muscles together in a clear example of active feedback.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the surface cells and then adding the outer layer felt somewhat repetitive, although both steps contributed to the skin model.

surprise.text: I was interested to learn that the outermost skin cells are dead and are replaced by living layers beneath.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the offered combinations had clear connections to the goals, though the later choices were the only combinations offered.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter if it offered another concrete activity like holding the glass; that outcome made the body systems feel connected.
